entities.name: Nikolaus von Jeroschin
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Nikolaus von Jeroschin, a Teutonic Knight and chaplain, emerged as a pivotal chronicler in the early 14th century, translating the Latin *Chronicon terrae Prussiae* by Peter von Dusburg into Middle High German verse. Born in an unknown location, his life culminated in 1341, having left an indelible mark on the historiography of the Teutonic Order's expansion into Prussia. Commissioned by Grand Master Luther von Braunschweig around 1330, von Jeroschin's work provided a vernacular account of the Order's crusades and territorial acquisitions, shaping the self-perception and external image of this powerful monastic-military institution during a critical period of its consolidation.

His magnum opus, known as the *Di Kronike von Prusen* (The Chronicle of Prussia), meticulously recounts the Order's history from its foundation up to the year 1330. While primarily an adaptation rather than an original composition, von Jeroschin's translation was not a mere transcription; he often expanded upon Dusburg's narrative, adding details, moralizing commentary, and poetic flourishes that resonated with a German-speaking aristocratic audience. The chronicle details the military campaigns, diplomatic maneuvers, and the establishment of towns and castles, providing a rich tapestry of the *Drang nach Osten* (push to the East) from the perspective of the crusaders themselves.
